# Internal Consistency and Conditional-Behaviour Checklist: Guided Bug Triage Run

**Purpose**: Interrogate whether the specification's conditional behaviour is stated as checkable outcomes rather than narrative, whether its skip and stop conditions are exhaustive over the outcomes they branch on, and whether its requirements agree with one another. Scoped to catch defects that the general spec-quality checklist passes.
**Created**: 2026-09-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Exhaustiveness of Conditional Branches

The specification branches on three recorded outcomes. Each branch is only as good as its coverage of the values that outcome can take.

- [x] CHK001 Does the spec state what the run does for **every** value the assessment's verdict can take, rather than only for the value that means "not a real defect"? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK002 Is the run's behaviour specified for an assessment verdict that is affirmative but conditional — one meaning the defect is probably real but has not been reproduced? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec state what the run does for **every** value the remediation stage's recorded status can take, rather than only for "skipped" and "no change applied"? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK004 Is the run's behaviour specified when remediation records that the change was applied only in part — as distinct from applied fully or not at all? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK005 Are the three outcome vocabularies the run branches on enumerated anywhere in the spec, so that a reader can tell whether a branch is exhaustive? [Gap, Traceability]
- [x] CHK006 Where the spec pairs a partial outcome with a non-partial one (FR-028 treats partial validation as unresolved), is the same pairing decision made or explicitly declined for the partial outcomes of the other two stages? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028]

## Skip and Stop Conditions

- [x] CHK007 For each stage that can be skipped, is the skip condition stated in terms of a value recorded in an artifact, rather than in terms of a judgement the run makes? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK008 Is it unambiguous which of "skip" and "stop" applies in each case, given that both leave a stage un-invoked but only one ends the run? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK009 Does the spec define what the run does after a stop — whether it may be resumed, restarted, or neither? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK010 Are the requirements for stopping consistent between an early stop chosen by the maintainer (FR-014) and a stop forced by an outcome (FR-010)? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK011 Is the behaviour specified for a maintainer who stops the run _after_ the remediation stage has already edited source files, a case the Edge Cases section raises but no requirement addresses? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Agreement Between Requirements

- [x] CHK012 Do FR-020's prohibition on committing and FR-030's obligation to name a commit workflow agree, or does one require what the other forbids? [Conflict, Spec §FR-020, §FR-030]
- [x] CHK013 Do FR-001's acceptance of a URL and FR-004's prohibition on retrieving one leave the run's obligations toward that URL fully determined? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-004]
- [x] CHK014 Is FR-022's instruction not to duplicate the underlying safety rules reconcilable with FR-004, which restates one of them? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-022]
- [x] CHK015 Does FR-019's requirement that nothing happen without approval define what counts as "something happening" — for instance whether reading the repository qualifies? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK016 Are the Assumptions' claim of an interactive-only run and the requirements' silence on any unattended mode consistent, given that the underlying capability behaves differently when it believes itself unattended? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Measurability of the Reporting Requirements

- [x] CHK017 Does the spec say how a stage's recorded outcome is to be located within that stage's report, or only that it must be taken from there? [Measurability, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK018 Can FR-015's "confirmed to exist" be objectively evaluated — is it existence of a file, non-emptiness, or well-formedness? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK019 Is SC-001's "without reading any other document" verifiable by someone reviewing a completed run, or does it require an observed trial with a naive user? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK020 Does SC-002's claim that refused invocations number zero depend on the branch coverage questioned in CHK001–CHK004 being complete? [Traceability, Spec §SC-002]

## Inputs, Identity and Scope Boundaries

- [x] CHK021 Is the source of the per-stage wording that FR-011 requires be shown to the maintainer identified anywhere — the run composes it, the maintainer supplies it, or it is fixed? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK022 Does the spec state how the run determines that the bug-triage capability is unavailable, as opposed to what it must do once it has determined that? [Gap, Spec §FR-023]
- [x] CHK023 Is the run's behaviour specified when the maintainer supplies more than one bug report, given that FR-021 states the limit but no requirement states the response to exceeding it? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021]
- [x] CHK024 Is the identifier-collision requirement in FR-003 consistent with FR-002's delegation of identifier derivation to the capability, whose own collision behaviour differs by mode? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]

## Terminology

- [x] CHK025 Is one term used consistently for the person the run addresses, rather than alternating between "maintainer", "caller" and "user"? [Consistency, Traceability]
- [x] CHK026 Are "stage" and the three stage names used consistently, without the underlying capability's own command vocabulary leaking into requirements that deliberately avoid it? [Consistency, Spec §Requirements]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference

This instrument was written to fail where `requirements.md` passes. That file asks whether requirements are testable and unambiguous in general; this one asks whether the specific branches the run takes are exhaustive over the values they branch on. CHK001–CHK004 are the items most likely to find something: the spec names two skip conditions, and the outcomes it skips on can each take three values.
